files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url` or `files`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so, unless it acts on what this session just found and so stays here), never what "Starting other sessions" keeps here or gives to a subagent; the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
schema.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so, unless it acts on what this session just found and so stays here), never what "Starting other sessions" keeps here or gives to a subagent; the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now (not for a piece "Starting other sessions" gives to a subagent). "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do, nor for the one piece of work "Starting other sessions" keeps here, nor for what it gives to a subagent. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session. Here and in `background`, put file paths and code identifiers in backticks.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one.

repository.description: With target "cloud", only when the user named a repository other than this project's: "owner/name" on github.com, which the cloud session clones at its default branch. Take the exact owner/name from the user's words or a listing that shows it; if you are not sure of it, ask them. A bypass or auto permission mode may not carry over: the session then starts in the cloud's default mode. If the call is refused, do not run or propose the other repository's work in this project.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

**このファイルが、記録 (管理のセッションが手元に持つファイル群) の置き場・様式・扱いの正本。** モジュール `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/record.py` と、CLI `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch.py` のサブコマンド `record read` / `record apply` / `record log` はこれに従う。ほかの文書はキーの名前を参照するだけで、様式と扱いを言い直さない。

**記録には、GitHub から導けないものだけを書く。** 導けるもの (下の「記録が持たないもの」) はターンのたびに GitHub から導く。記録と GitHub が食い違う場面と、記録を失ったときに作り直す別の手順を無くすため。

## 置き場

`<管理ディレクトリ>/<record_dir>/<owner>-<number>/`。`record_dir` は管理ディレクトリの設定のキー (デフォルト値はキーの表 [project-config.md](project-config.md) が持つ)。`<owner>-<number>` は設定の `project` から作る。置き場を Project ごとに分けるのは、設定の `project` を後で別の Project に書き換えたときに、前の Project の記録と混ざらないようにするため。置き場は git が無視する (設定は追跡し、記録は追跡しない)。

| ファイル | 書き手 | 内容 | 様式の正本 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record.json` | 管理のセッション (CLI の `record apply`) | 本体。下の「`record.json`」 | この文書 |
| `actions.log` | 管理のセッション (CLI の `record log`) | GitHub への書き込みの追記専用のログ。下の「`actions.log`」 | この文書 |
| `snapshot.json` | 管理のセッション (観測の単位) | ポーリングの基準になる Project の状態の写し。作り直せるキャッシュ | [observation.md](observation.md) |
| `wait.pid` | 待機のスクリプト | 実行中の待機の PID・開始時刻・所有者のセッション ID | [observation.md](observation.md) |

**書き手は管理のセッション (とそのスクリプト) だけ。** 作業のセッションは記録を持たない。

## 一時名と改名

ほかのプロセス (待機のスクリプトなど) が読むファイルは、同じディレクトリの一時名 (`.` で始まり `.tmp` で終わる名前) に書いてから `os.replace` (改名) で置き換える。同じファイルシステムの中の改名は一度に起きるので、読む側が書きかけを読むことが無く、書く途中で失敗しても元のファイルが残る。`record.json` の保存はこの形で行い、`actions.log` は追記だけなので一時名を使わない。

## 種類ごとの扱い

データは「壊れていたときに何が失われるか」で種類を分け、読めない・壊れているときの振る舞いを種類ごとに決める (考え方の正本は `docs/solutions/architecture-patterns/fail-soft-by-data-class.md`)。

| 種類 | ファイル | 失われるもの | 読めない・壊れているとき |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 設定 | `config.json` | 利用者が書いた数行 | デフォルト値で続けて警告する ([project-config.md](project-config.md)) |
| 記録 | `record.json` | 割り当ての意図・問いと答え・印 (作り直せない) | 止めて知らせ、新規として扱わない (`Corrupt`)。無いときだけ新規 |
| スナップショット | `snapshot.json` | 無い (Project から導出し直せる) | 作り直して 1 行報告する |
| ログ | `actions.log` | 書き込みの履歴 | 読まない (追記だけ)。壊れた行は読む側が飛ばす |
| 宣言 (エージェントが組み立てる入力) | Issue のコメント | その 1 件 | 形を検査して差し戻す ([issue-format.md](issue-format.md)) |

壊れた記録を新規として扱わないのは、新規の記録を保存すると元の記録 (割り当ての意図や問いの答え) を失うため。壊れていれば利用者に知らせ、利用者がバックアップから戻すか消すかを決める。

## `record.json`

トップレベルのキー:

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | `owner/number`。設定の `project` と違えば壊れているとみなす (別の Project の記録を読まないため) |
| `manager` | 管理のセッション (下の表)。開始前は null |
| `sessions` | 作業のセッションの ID → 下の表 |
| `items` | 項目 (`owner/repo#番号`) → 下の表。項目が属する作業のセッションは記録に持たず、Project のフィールド `Agent session ID` から導く |
| `opt_in_proposals` | リポジトリ (`owner/repo`) → 第三者による本文の編集の確認のオプトインの提案 (`proposed_at` 提案した時刻・`answer` 答え。未回答は null) |
| `notices` | 項目に紐づかない「1 回だけ報告する」知らせの印。知らせの名前 → 報告した時刻 |
| `questions` | 問いの ID → 下の表 |

`manager`:

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `id` / `name` | 管理のセッションの ID と名前 |
| `started_at` | 開始した時刻 |
| `state` | `active` (動いている)・`stopped` (停止)・`ended` (終了) |
| `stop_reason` | 停止の理由。`active` では null |
| `exchanges_since_input` | 利用者の最後の入力からの送受の数 (R9)。利用者の入力で 0 に戻す |

`sessions` の要素 (作業のセッション):

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `name` / `repo` / `worktree` | 名前・リポジトリ (`owner/repo`)・作業ツリーの絶対パス |
| `seen_state` | 前のターンに `ListAgents` で見た状態 (R10 の `waiting-for-user` の判断に使う)。未確認は null |
| `waiting_since` | 待機中なら待機を始めた時刻。待機中でなければ null |
| `refused` | 合図を受信拒否された最初の記録 (`at` 時刻・`signal` 合図の種類)。無ければ null。以後の送り方と戻し方は、スキル `issue-work` と `issue-dispatch` の手順で決める (Open Questions の R9 (2) の項) |

`items` の要素 (項目):

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `intent` | 割り当ての書き込みの意図 (`session_id`・`session_title`・`status` に書く予定の値、`assignment` 割り当ての番号、`at` 決めた時刻)。無ければ null。Project の値が意図と一致すれば自分の書き込みと判定する (再入の部分完了の続き。R24) |
| `notified_at` | 合図 `assigned` を送った印 (時刻)。意図があって印が無い項目は、再入で合図を送り直す候補。同じ印を 2 度付けても最初の時刻のまま。いつ付くかの正本は [flow.md](flow.md) |
| `resend_count` | 合図の再送の回数。再送は項目ごとに通算 1 回で、1 回再送した後は再送しない (R24)。再送の前に回数を確かめ、再送したら数える |
| `conflict_choice` | 競合の可能性があるときに選んだ扱い |
| `reported` | 報告済みの印。報告の種類 (人の変更・割り当てない理由など) → 最初に報告した時刻 |
| `body_edit_confirmed_at` | 利用者が確かめた本文の最新の編集の時刻 (KD17) |

`questions` の要素 (問い):

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `item` / `kind` | 問いの対象の項目と種類 |
| `options` | 選択肢の配列。要素は空でない文字列で、重複しない (答えは選択肢と同じ文字列で照合する)。空なら自由回答 |
| `asked_at` | 尋ねた時刻 |
| `answer` / `answered_at` | 答えと答えた時刻。未回答はどちらも null。取り下げた問い (`withdraw`) は `answer` が null で `answered_at` がある |

問いの種類 (`kind`) と選択肢 (`options`)。導くのは項目の状態 ([flow.md](flow.md) の「ターンで行うこと」)。答えに従う処理は U15・U16・U21 で決める。

| 種類 | 尋ねること | 選択肢 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close-in-progress` | 進行中の Issue が閉じられた。作業のセッションに止めるよう伝えるか、reopen して続けるか | `stop` / `reopen` |
| `assignee-changed` | 割り当て中の項目の担当者が自分 1 人でなくなった。割り当てを解除するか、そのまま続けるか | `release` / `continue` |
| `field-cleared` | `Agent session ID` が空にされた。解除するか、書き戻すか | `release` / `restore` |
| `field-changed` | `Agent session ID` が別の値にされた。解除するか、書き戻すか | `release` / `restore` |
| `removed` | 割り当て中の項目が Project から除かれた。解除するか、持ち続けるか | `release` / `keep` |
| `status-changed` | 割り当て中の項目の Status を手で変えられた。解除するか、Status を戻すか | `release` / `restore` |
| `third-party-edit` | 確認の対象の項目の本文を、割り当ての後に第三者が編集した。作業のセッションに止めるよう伝えてよいか | `stop` / `continue` |
| `merged-issue-open` | PR がマージされたが Issue が開いている。閉じるか | `close` / `keep` |
| `pr-closed-unmerged` | PR がマージされずに閉じた。Status を戻して解除するか | `release` / `keep` |
| `user-answer-lost` | 記録を失ったので、`利用者の答え` を待っていた宣言の問いを尋ね直す (自由回答) | 無し |

### 操作 (`record apply`)

`record.json` は、操作の配列を標準入力で受ける CLI の `record apply` で更新する。1 ターンの複数の更新を 1 回の保存にまとめ、**1 つでも誤りがあれば何も適用せず、誤りを返す** (部分的に適用すると、意図と印の対応が崩れるため)。各操作は `op` と、種類ごとのキーを持つ。項目のキー `item` は `owner/repo#番号` の形。時刻は呼び出し側が書く (ISO 8601、UTC)。

| `op` | キー | 何をするか |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_manager` | `id`・`name`・`started_at` | 管理のセッションを `active` で記録する。送受の数は 0 |

    コメントより後に Status の変化があれば利用者の変更として報告する。返り値は (actions, reports)。"""
    status = (item.get("status") or {}).get("name")
    if state.get("assigned") or not _in_scope(item, login) or status not in STATUS_OPTIONS_FOR_DEPENDENCY:

宣言の判定 (issue-dispatch U15) の案

宣言の判定 (issue-dispatch U15) の案

U15 (判定) の前提・判定の内容・順序・決定したいこと。図の矢印は「行う・使用する」の向き。

mermaid の読み込みに失敗しました。CDN への到達 (ネットワーク) を確認してください。図のソースは下にテキストのまま表示されています。

1. 前提

issue-dispatch は、GitHub Project の Issue を複数の Claude Code のセッションに割り当てて並行に作業させる仕組み。セッションは 2 種類ある。管理のセッションは Project を定期的に読み、Issue の割り当てと、作業の衝突を避けるための判定を行う (1 つ)。作業のセッションは割り当てられた Issue の作業を行う (複数)。利用者は管理のセッションの会話で質問に回答する。

作業のセッションは、作業を始める前に「変更する予定のファイルと節と資源」を宣言し、管理のセッションの判定 (ほかの作業と競合しうるか・資源が空いているか) を待機する。判定の結果が出るまで作業を始めない。U15 は、この判定を行う部分。

登場するもの

登場するもの | どこにあるか | 役割 | 

作業のセッション | Claude Code のセッション (複数) | 宣言を投稿し、判定の結果を待機し、結果に従って作業を始める・待機する・宣言を書き直す | 

管理のセッション | Claude Code のセッション (1 つ) | Project とコメントを読み、宣言を判定し、結果をコメント・Status・合図で返す。利用者に質問する | 

利用者 | 管理のセッションの会話 | 管理のセッションの質問に回答する (競合しうるときの扱いなど)。回答は記録に保存される | 

宣言 (コメント 着手の宣言 / 宣言の更新) | Issue のコメント (作業のセッションが投稿) | 判定の対象。本文に JSON (files: パスと節、resources: 使用する資源、split: 分割の提案) | 

判定の結果 (コメント 開始可 / 待機 / 依頼) | Issue のコメント (管理のセッションが投稿) | 判定した宣言の ID を持つ。開始可 は作業を始めてよい、待機 は理由 (利用者の回答・Issue・小さな PR・資源・設定) が解消するまで待機、依頼 は宣言の書き直しなどの依頼 | 

合図 | セッション間のメッセージ (Claude Code の SendMessage) | 相手を起こすための通知。種類は下の表。失われても GitHub 上の対応物 (コメント・Status) で検出できるので、観測を早めるだけ | 

作業のセッションの待機 (wait-decision) | 作業のセッションのバックグラウンドのプロセス (U14) | 自分の宣言への 開始可・待機 (管理のセッションが書いた Blocked)・依頼 を定期的に読んで検出し、作業のセッションを起こす | 

Status・blockedBy | GitHub Project の項目と Issue | 待機 の理由が Issue か小さな PR のとき、管理のセッションが相手の Issue を blockedBy に追加して Status を Blocked にする (解消したら In Progress に戻す) | 

記録 (record.json) | 管理ディレクトリ (管理のセッションのローカル) | GitHub から導出できないもの: 利用者への質問と回答、競合しうるときに選択した扱い (conflict_choice) など | 

リポジトリの設定 (ファイルの種類の規則) | 元の clone の既定のブランチ (管理のセッションが git で読む) | ファイルの種類 (generated・divisible など) を決める規則。読めなければ判定を停止する | 

合図の種類

合図 | 向き | 意味 | GitHub 上の対応物 | 

declared | 作業 → 管理 | 宣言を投稿した (判定を求める) | コメント 着手の宣言 / 宣言の更新 | 

go | 管理 → 作業 | 作業を始めてよい | コメント 開始可 (待機していた Issue の再開では Status In Progress も) | 

wait | 管理 → 作業 | 待機する (理由を含む) | コメント 待機・blockedBy・Status Blocked (資源の待機ではコメントだけ) | 

request | 管理 → 作業 | 依頼 (宣言の書き直し・PR の本文の追記・小さな PR の作成) | コメント 依頼 | 

用語

用語 | 意味 | 

競合の可能性 | 2 つの宣言が、同じリポジトリの同じファイルの同じ節 (または節を書いていないファイル全体) を変更する予定で、マージで衝突しうること。判定の規則は U10 (ファイルの種類ごと)。結果は conflict (競合しうる)・none (競合しない)・needs-user (利用者の判定が要る) | 

unknown-content | ファイルの種類の 1 つ。パスがどの規則にも一致せず内容を知らないファイル。同じパスなら、競合しうるかどうかを利用者に質問する | 

競合しうるときの 3 つの扱い | 利用者が選択する: 相手の Issue の完了まで待機する (wait) / 共通の変更だけを先に小さな PR にする (small-pr) / 競合しうるまま進める (proceed。衝突は利用者が解消する) | 

小さな PR | 先に 開始可 になった作業のセッションが、競合しうるファイルの変更だけを別のブランチの PR にして先にマージするもの。待機する側はその PR のマージまで待機する。依頼先の Issue にコメント 小さな PR の報告 で PR の URL が報告される | 

資源 | 同時に使用できる数が限られるもの (検証用の DB など)。Issue のラベル resource:<名前> と宣言の resources で表す。属性 when_busy (空いていないとき待機するか利用者に質問するか) と release_undeclared (割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源を解放するか質問するか) は管理ディレクトリの設定 (U11) | 

判定の要る宣言 | 着手の宣言と宣言の更新のうち、資源を外すだけの更新を除いたもの。U13 の導出が、項目ごとに最新の判定の要る宣言と、その段階 (未判定・開始可・待機・差し戻し) を返す | 

In review | PR が ready for review になった後の Status。この後の宣言の更新は資源だけを判定する | 

判定の流れ

sequenceDiagram
    participant W as 作業のセッション
    participant I as Issue のコメント
    participant P as Project / Issue
    participant M as 管理のセッション
    participant U as 利用者
    W->>I: 着手の宣言 を投稿
    W->>M: 合図 declared
    M->>I: 宣言を読む
    M->>M: 判定 (競合の可能性・資源・設定)
    alt 競合しない
        M->>I: 開始可 を投稿
        M->>W: 合図 go
    else 競合しうる
        M->>I: 待機 (理由 利用者の回答) を投稿
        M->>U: 質問: 3 つの扱いのどれにするか
        U->>M: 回答 (例: 相手の完了まで待機)
        M->>I: 待機 (理由 Issue) を投稿
        M->>P: blockedBy を追加し Blocked にする
        M->>W: 合図 wait
    else 形式の誤り
        M->>I: 依頼 (宣言の書き直し) を投稿
        M->>W: 合図 request
    end

既に実装済みのもの: 競合の可能性の判定そのもの (U10 の declaration.conflictability)、資源の判定 (U11 の resources.judge_declare など)、項目の状態の導出 (U13 の itemstate: どの宣言が未判定か・何を待機しているか)、待機 (U14)。U15 はこれらを結合して「どの順序で、何と比較して、何を書くか」を決める。

2. 1 件の判定

宣言 1 件の判定は、次の順序で分岐し、結果を go (開始可)・wait (待機。理由付き)・ask (利用者に質問し、回答まで 待機。理由は利用者の回答)・request (書き直しの依頼) の 4 つのどれかに決める。各分岐の条件と値の範囲は図の下の表。

flowchart TB
    s0["宣言を読む"] --> s1{"リポジトリの設定を読めるか"}
    s1 -->|読めない| w1["wait: 理由 設定"]
    s1 -->|読める| s2{"宣言の形式は正しいか"}
    s2 -->|誤り| r1["request: 宣言の書き直し"]
    s2 -->|正しい| s3{"競合の可能性の結果に conflict があるか"}
    s3 -->|ある| q1{"記録に、その相手への回答があるか"}
    q1 -->|無い| a1["ask: 3 つの扱い"]
    q1 -->|ある| v1{"回答の値"}
    v1 -->|wait| w2["wait: 理由 Issue (相手)"]
    v1 -->|small-pr| w3["wait: 理由 小さな PR + request: 相手に小さな PR の依頼"]
    v1 -->|proceed| s4
    s3 -->|無い| s3b{"結果に needs-user があるか"}
    s3b -->|ある| q2{"記録に、そのパスへの回答があるか"}
    q2 -->|無い| a2["ask: unknown-content のパスが競合しうるか"]
    q2 -->|ある| v2{"回答の値"}
    v2 -->|conflict| q1
    v2 -->|none| s4
    s3b -->|無い| s4{"宣言の新しい資源はすべて空いているか"}
    s4 -->|空いている| s6
    s4 -->|空いていない資源がある| s5{"その資源の when_busy の値"}
    s5 -->|wait| w4["wait: 理由 資源"]
    s5 -->|ask| q3{"記録に、その資源への回答があるか"}
    q3 -->|無い| a3["ask: 資源が使用中。待機するか進めるか"]
    q3 -->|ある| v3{"回答の値"}
    v3 -->|wait| w4
    v3 -->|proceed| s6{"割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源があるか"}
    s6 -->|無い| g1["go: 開始可"]
    s6 -->|ある| s7{"その資源の release_undeclared の値"}
    s7 -->|release| g2["go: 開始可 (その予約を解放する)"]
    s7 -->|ask| q4{"記録に、その資源への回答があるか"}
    q4 -->|無い| g3["go: 開始可 (予約は残す) + ask: 解放してよいか"]
    q4 -->|ある| v4{"回答の値"}
    v4 -->|release| g2
    v4 -->|keep| r2["request: 資源を追加した宣言の書き直し (予約は残す)"]

分岐 | 条件 | 取りうる値 | 出所 | 

リポジトリの設定を読めるか | U6 の repo.read_repo_config の status | ok (設定あり) / missing (既定のブランチに設定ファイルが無い。デフォルトの表だけで照合し、「読める」として進む) / unreadable (読めない) | 元の clone の既定のブランチ | 

宣言の形式は正しいか | declaration.parse の status | ok / error (必須キーの欠落・未知のキー・パスの誤り・節の表記の無いファイルの units など。誤りは全部集める) | 宣言の JSON | 

競合の可能性の結果 | declaration.conflictability の全体の結論。相手ごと・パスごとの結果を conflict > needs-user > none の順で集約する | conflict / needs-user / none の 3 値。図では「conflict があるか」「needs-user があるか」の順に見る (conflict の相手が 1 つでもあれば先に 3 つの扱いを質問し、needs-user だけなら unknown-content の判定を質問する)。unknown-content の判定で利用者が「競合しうる」と回答したときは、その相手について 3 つの扱いの分岐 (q1) に進む (判定の分岐 s3 には戻らない) | 宣言と 開始可 の宣言 | 

記録に回答があるか (競合・unknown-content・資源) | 記録の質問のうち、同じ項目・同じ種類・同じ対象 (相手の宣言・パス・資源の名前) で、answer が null でないものがあるか。取り下げた質問 (withdraw。answer は null) は「無い」に数える | ある / 無い | 記録 record.json | 

回答の値 | その質問の回答 (選択肢の 1 つ) | 競合: wait / small-pr / proceed、unknown-content: conflict / none、資源: wait / proceed、解放: release / keep (記録の操作 answer は選択肢に無い値を拒否する) | 記録 record.json | 

宣言の新しい資源はすべて空いているか | 宣言の resources のうち、割り当てで予約していない資源について、持つ項目の数が capacity 未満か | すべて空いている / 空いていない資源が 1 つ以上ある (1 つでも空いていなければ、空いている資源も予約しない) | U13 の資源の使用 (usage) と U11 の属性 | 

when_busy の値 | 資源の属性 (設定の resources) | wait / ask の 2 値。設定に無い資源と書かれていない属性はデフォルト値 wait。それ以外の値は設定の読み込みで警告してデフォルト値に直す | 管理ディレクトリの設定 | 

割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源があるか | 割り当ての時点のラベルの資源 (U13 の reserved) のうち、宣言の resources に無いもの | 無い / ある | U13 の導出 | 

release_undeclared の値 | 資源の属性 | release / ask の 2 値 (デフォルト値 ask。それ以外は警告してデフォルト値) | 管理ディレクトリの設定 | 

補足: 資源の分岐 (s4 以降) は、競合の可能性で wait / ask になった宣言には進まない (待機中の宣言は新しい資源を持たない。U11)。release_undeclared の質問は、ほかの判定が済んでいれば 開始可 を書いてから行い、回答が出るまでその予約を残す (計画の KTD8)。開始可 を書く直前には、節 3 の再比較をもう 1 度行う。

比較の相手は、既に 開始可 になった宣言だけ (未判定の宣言どうしは比較しない)。In review の PR が変更した、宣言に無いファイルも相手に加える (U13 の照合)。

3. 判定の順序と、開始可 を書く直前の再比較

未判定の宣言が複数あれば、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定する。利用者の回答を待機する間に時間が経つと、その間に 開始可 になった宣言とは比較していないので、どの経路 (判定の直後・回答の後・待機の解消の後・資源の解放の後) で 開始可 を書くときも、直前にその時点の 開始可 の宣言すべてと再比較する。新しく競合しうる相手があれば 開始可 を書かず、その相手について節 2 の q1 (回答があるか) に進む。例外は ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新で、ファイルの競合の可能性を判定しないので再比較しない。

4. 待機の解消と再判定 (後半)

待機 中の宣言は、理由ごとに解消を検出し、解消した宣言を投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に再判定する。再判定は節 2 の判定をやり直すこと (直前の再比較を含む) で、相手は再判定の時点の 開始可 の宣言すべて。先に投稿された宣言を再判定する前に、後に投稿された 開始可 の宣言も相手に入れる (入れずに再判定すると、競合しうるのに質問せずに 開始可 を書くため)。

待機の理由 | 解消の条件 | 検出の出所 | 

Issue (相手の完了を待機) | 相手の Issue の割り当てが終了した (進行中の close で利用者の回答を待機する間は終了していない) | U13 の end | 

小さな PR | 小さな PR がマージされた。または依頼先の Issue の割り当てが終了した。マージされずに閉じたときは利用者に質問 | 小さな PR の報告 の PR の状態 | 

資源 | その資源が解放された (宣言の更新・Issue の close・割り当ての解除) | U13 の usage | 

設定 | リポジトリの設定が読めるようになった | 再入のたびに読み直す | 

利用者の回答 | 記録に回答が入った | 記録 record.json | 

5. 決定したいこと

質問 1: 判定を待機している宣言が書き直されたとき、前の宣言の待機を新しい宣言が継承するか

前提: 作業のセッションは、判定の結果 (開始可) が出る前に宣言を書き直すことがある (管理のセッションが 依頼 で書き直しを求めたとき。release_undeclared の回答 keep による書き直しは、節 2 のとおり 開始可 を書いた後に出ることが多いが、ほかの判定が済まず 開始可 の前に回答が出たときはこの前提に含む)。判定の結果 (開始可・待機・依頼) と小さな PR の依頼と報告は、宣言のコメントの ID で対応づけるので、書き直すと ID が変わる。

問題: 前の宣言で利用者が選択した扱い (待機 / 小さな PR / そのまま進める)・追加した blockedBy・出した小さな PR の依頼を、新しい宣言にどう引き継ぐか決まっていない。引き継がないと同じ質問を繰り返し、引き継ぐと新しい宣言の内容 (相手が変わりうる) と合わない扱いを続ける。

案: 同じ相手との競合の可能性には、前の宣言への conflict の質問の回答 (記録。質問 3 の subject で相手を区別する) を使用して再度質問しない。新しい相手だけ質問する。小さな PR の依頼は、新しい宣言でも同じ相手と競合しうるなら、新しい宣言への 待機 に前の依頼先 (報告済みなら PR も) を転記し、新しい依頼は出さない (報告は前の宣言の ID で対応づけたまま読む)。前の 待機 のために追加した blockedBy は、新しい判定でも同じ相手を待機するなら残し、そうでなければ削除の候補にする。

前提: 記録の質問は kind と選択肢 (options) を持ち、U13 で項目の状態の質問の種類 (close-in-progress など、英語) を records.md の表に定めた。

質問 3: 質問の対象の記載方法

前提: 記録の質問は item・kind・options・asked_at・answer・answered_at だけを持つ (U5)。

問題: 資源の質問は資源の名前を、競合の質問は相手の宣言の ID を保持しないと、回答をどの資源・どの相手に適用するか分からない。同じ項目に資源の質問が 2 つ (資源 DB と GPU) あることもある。

案: 記録の質問に任意のキー subject (文字列。資源の名前、相手の項目と宣言の ID など) を追加する。U5 の record.py と records.md を修正する (withdraw を追加したときと同じ扱い)。U5 にある項目ごとの conflict_choice (相手を持たない) は、競合しうるときの扱いの保存先としては使わず、conflict の質問の回答 (相手ごと) で代える (conflict_choice は残すが書かない。消すかは U21 で決める)。

質問 4: declaration judge の出力の形式

前提: U13 の item state は、書き込みの候補 actions・質問 questions・報告 reports を返し、CLI 自身は書き込まない。書き込みは管理のセッションのスキル (U21・U23) が既存のサブコマンドで行う。

案: 同じ形式にそろえ、judgments (宣言ごとの結果と理由)・actions・questions・signals (送信する合図 go / wait / request と宛先。送信方法は U17) を返す。

競合の可能性の結果 | declaration.conflictability の全体の結論。相手ごと・パスごとの結果を conflict > needs-user > none の順で集約する | conflict / needs-user / none の 3 値。図では「conflict があるか」「needs-user があるか」の順に見る (conflict の相手が 1 つでもあれば先に 3 つの扱いを質問し、needs-user だけなら unknown-content の判定を質問する)。unknown-content の判定で利用者が「競合しうる」と回答したときは、その相手について 3 つの扱いの分岐 (q1) に進む (判定の分岐 s3 には戻らない) | 宣言と 開始可 の宣言 | 

記録に回答があるか (競合・unknown-content・資源) | 記録の質問のうち、同じ項目・同じ種類・同じ対象 (相手の宣言・パス・資源の名前) で、answer が null でないものがあるか。取り下げた質問 (withdraw。answer は null) は「無い」に数える | ある / 無い | 記録 record.json | 

回答の値 | その質問の回答 (選択肢の 1 つ) | 競合: wait / small-pr / proceed、unknown-content: conflict / none、資源: wait / proceed、解放: release / keep (記録の操作 answer は選択肢に無い値を拒否する) | 記録 record.json | 

宣言の新しい資源はすべて空いているか | 宣言の resources のうち、割り当てで予約していない資源について、持つ項目の数が capacity 未満か | すべて空いている / 空いていない資源が 1 つ以上ある (1 つでも空いていなければ、空いている資源も予約しない) | U13 の資源の使用 (usage) と U11 の属性 | 

when_busy の値 | 資源の属性 (設定の resources) | wait / ask の 2 値。設定に無い資源と書かれていない属性はデフォルト値 wait。それ以外の値は設定の読み込みで警告してデフォルト値に直す | 管理ディレクトリの設定 | 

割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源があるか | 割り当ての時点のラベルの資源 (U13 の reserved) のうち、宣言の resources に無いもの | 無い / ある | U13 の導出 | 

release_undeclared の値 | 資源の属性 | release / ask の 2 値 (デフォルト値 ask。それ以外は警告してデフォルト値) | 管理ディレクトリの設定 | 

補足: 資源の分岐 (s4 以降) は、競合の可能性で wait / ask になった宣言には進まない (待機中の宣言は新しい資源を持たない。U11)。release_undeclared の質問は、ほかの判定が済んでいれば 開始可 を書いてから行い、回答が出るまでその予約を残す (計画の KTD8)。開始可 を書く直前には、節 3 の再比較をもう 1 度行う。

比較の相手は、既に 開始可 になった宣言だけ (未判定の宣言どうしは比較しない)。In review の PR が変更した、宣言に無いファイルも相手に加える (U13 の照合)。

3. 判定の順序と、開始可 を書く直前の再比較

未判定の宣言が複数あれば、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定する。利用者の回答を待機する間に時間が経つと、その間に 開始可 になった宣言とは比較していないので、どの経路 (判定の直後・回答の後・待機の解消の後・資源の解放の後) で 開始可 を書くときも、直前にその時点の 開始可 の宣言すべてと再比較する。新しく競合しうる相手があれば 開始可 を書かず、その相手について節 2 の q1 (回答があるか) に進む。例外は ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新で、ファイルの競合の可能性を判定しないので再比較しない。

sequenceDiagram
    participant M as 管理のセッション
    participant I as Issue のコメント
    participant U as 利用者
    Note over M,U: A・B・C が同じファイルを変更する宣言を、この順に投稿した
    M->>I: A を判定: 相手なし → 開始可
    M->>I: B を判定: A と競合しうる → 待機 (利用者の回答)
    M->>I: C を判定: A と競合しうる → 待機 (利用者の回答)
    M->>U: 質問: B と C の扱い
    U->>M: B も C も 待機 を選択
    M->>I: B: 待機 (理由 Issue A)、C: 待機 (理由 Issue A)
    Note over M,I: A の割り当てが終了した (Issue の正常な終わり。節 4 の表)
    M->>I: B を再判定: 相手なし → 開始可 (直前の再比較: 相手なし)
    M->>I: C を再判定: B と競合しうる (相手が変わった)
    M->>U: 再度質問: C の扱い (相手は B)

4. 待機の解消と再判定 (後半)

待機 中の宣言は、理由ごとに解消を検出し、解消した宣言を投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に再判定する。再判定は節 2 の判定をやり直すこと (直前の再比較を含む) で、相手は再判定の時点の 開始可 の宣言すべて。先に投稿された宣言を再判定する前に、後に投稿された 開始可 の宣言も相手に入れる (入れずに再判定すると、競合しうるのに質問せずに 開始可 を書くため)。

待機の理由 | 解消の条件 | 検出の出所 | 

Issue (相手の完了を待機) | 相手の Issue の割り当てが終了した (進行中の close で利用者の回答を待機する間は終了していない) | U13 の end | 

小さな PR | 小さな PR がマージされた。または依頼先の Issue の割り当てが終了した。マージされずに閉じたときは利用者に質問 | 小さな PR の報告 の PR の状態 | 

資源 | その資源が解放された (宣言の更新・Issue の close・割り当ての解除) | U13 の usage | 

設定 | リポジトリの設定が読めるようになった | 再入のたびに読み直す | 

利用者の回答 | 記録に回答が入った | 記録 record.json | 

5. 決定したいこと

質問 1: 判定を待機している宣言が書き直されたとき、前の宣言の待機を新しい宣言が継承するか

前提: 作業のセッションは、判定の結果 (開始可) が出る前に宣言を書き直すことがある (管理のセッションが 依頼 で書き直しを求めたとき。release_undeclared の回答 keep による書き直しは、節 2 のとおり 開始可 を書いた後に出ることが多いが、ほかの判定が済まず 開始可 の前に回答が出たときはこの前提に含む)。判定の結果 (開始可・待機・依頼) と小さな PR の依頼と報告は、宣言のコメントの ID で対応づけるので、書き直すと ID が変わる。

問題: 前の宣言で利用者が選択した扱い (待機 / 小さな PR / そのまま進める)・追加した blockedBy・出した小さな PR の依頼を、新しい宣言にどう引き継ぐか決まっていない。引き継がないと同じ質問を繰り返し、引き継ぐと新しい宣言の内容 (相手が変わりうる) と合わない扱いを続ける。

案: 同じ相手との競合の可能性には、前の宣言への conflict の質問の回答 (記録。質問 3 の subject で相手を区別する) を使用して再度質問しない。新しい相手だけ質問する。小さな PR の依頼は、新しい宣言でも同じ相手と競合しうるなら、新しい宣言への 待機 に前の依頼先 (報告済みなら PR も) を転記し、新しい依頼は出さない (報告は前の宣言の ID で対応づけたまま読む)。前の 待機 のために追加した blockedBy は、新しい判定でも同じ相手を待機するなら残し、そうでなければ削除の候補にする。

flowchart LR
    d1["宣言 ID 400: A と競合 → 利用者が 待機 を選択 → blockedBy A"]
    d2["宣言 ID 401 (書き直し)"]
    d1 -->|書き直し| d2
    d2 --> q{"新しい宣言も A と競合しうるか"}
    q -->|はい| k["前の回答を使用: 待機 のまま。質問しない。blockedBy A を残す"]
    q -->|いいえ| q2{"ほかの相手 (B など) と競合しうるか"}
    q2 -->|はい| n["B について質問する。blockedBy A は削除の候補"]
    q2 -->|いいえ| g["開始可 (直前の再比較の後)。blockedBy A は削除の候補"]

質問 2: 判定の質問の種類の名前

前提: 記録の質問は kind と選択肢 (options) を持ち、U13 で項目の状態の質問の種類 (close-in-progress など、英語) を records.md の表に定めた。

案: 判定の質問も英語で追加する: conflict (wait / small-pr / proceed)・unknown-content (conflict / none)・resource-busy (wait / proceed)・release-undeclared (release / keep)・small-pr-closed (wait-issue / redo / proceed)。

質問 3: 質問の対象の記載方法

前提: 記録の質問は item・kind・options・asked_at・answer・answered_at だけを持つ (U5)。

問題: 資源の質問は資源の名前を、競合の質問は相手の宣言の ID を保持しないと、回答をどの資源・どの相手に適用するか分からない。同じ項目に資源の質問が 2 つ (資源 DB と GPU) あることもある。

案: 記録の質問に任意のキー subject (文字列。資源の名前、相手の項目と宣言の ID など) を追加する。U5 の record.py と records.md を修正する (withdraw を追加したときと同じ扱い)。U5 にある項目ごとの conflict_choice (相手を持たない) は、競合しうるときの扱いの保存先としては使わず、conflict の質問の回答 (相手ごと) で代える (conflict_choice は残すが書かない。消すかは U21 で決める)。

質問 4: declaration judge の出力の形式

前提: U13 の item state は、書き込みの候補 actions・質問 questions・報告 reports を返し、CLI 自身は書き込まない。書き込みは管理のセッションのスキル (U21・U23) が既存のサブコマンドで行う。

案: 同じ形式にそろえ、judgments (宣言ごとの結果と理由)・actions・questions・signals (送信する合図 go / wait / request と宛先。送信方法は U17) を返す。

6. 質問

質問 1〜4 の案でよいか。変更したいものがあれば番号で。

作る順序 (前半: 1 件の判定と書き込みの一覧、後半: 待機の解消と再判定) でよいか。

"""項目の状態 (itemstate) のテスト。導出は gh を実行しないので、項目は合成して渡す (コメントの先頭行は comments.format_header で作る)。
CLI のテストは偽の gh (tests/fake-gh) と固定データで動く。場面はテストの名前に書く (計画の U13)。"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_SCRIPTS = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "scripts")
sys.path.insert(0, _SCRIPTS)
sys.path.insert(0, _HERE)

from issue_dispatch import comments, config, itemstate  # noqa: E402
from test_project import FakeGhCase, fixture_json  # noqa: E402

_CLI = os.path.join(_SCRIPTS, "issue_dispatch.py")
_DOC = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "skills", "issue-dispatch", "references", "flow.md")
A = "akm/issue-dispatch-verify-a"
A1, A2, A9 = f"{A}#1", f"{A}#2", f"{A}#9"
LOGIN = "akm"
W7, M1 = "W-7", "M-1"
PR9 = f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/9"
PR10 = f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/10"
PROJECT_NUMBER = 3
_T = ["2026-10-20T00:00:00Z"]


def t(minutes):
    """基準から minutes 分後の時刻 (ISO 8601、UTC)。"""
    return f"2026-10-20T{minutes // 60:02d}:{minutes % 60:02d}:00Z"


def mcomment(kind, values=None, at=None, cid=None, body="", role="manager", name="mgr", sid=M1, author=LOGIN):
    """先頭行付きのコメント (project.items の comments の要素の形)。"""
    line = comments.format_header(role, name, sid, kind, values or {})
    return {"id": f"IC_{cid}", "database_id": cid, "url": f"https://github.com/{A}/issues/9#issuecomment-{cid}",
            "created_at": at, "author": author, "body": f"{line}\n\n{body}" if body else line}


def wcomment(kind, values=None, at=None, cid=None, body="", name="worker 1", sid=W7, author=LOGIN):
    return mcomment(kind, values, at, cid, body, role="worker", name=name, sid=sid, author=author)


def decl_body(files=(("src/a.py", None),), resources=(), split=False):
    obj = {"files": [{"path": p, "units": u} for p, u in files], "resources": list(resources),
           "split": {"needed": True, "reason": "大きい", "remaining": "残り", "blocked_by": []} if split else {"needed": False, "reason": ""}}
    return "```json\n" + json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n```"


def make_item(key=A9, state="OPEN", status="In Progress", session_field=W7, comments_=(), events=(), prs=(), labels=(), assignees=("akm",),
              body_edits=(), position=1, blocked_by=()):
    return {"item_id": "I9", "position": position, "key": key, "repo": key.split("#")[0], "number": int(key.split("#")[1]),
            "url": f"https://github.com/{key.replace('#', '/issues/')}", "state": state, "created_at": t(0), "author": "akm",
            "status": {"name": status, "option_id": "o", "updated_at": t(1)} if status else None,
            "fields": {"Agent session ID": {"text": session_field, "updated_at": t(1)}} if session_field is not None else {},
            "assignees": list(assignees), "labels": list(labels), "blocked_by": list(blocked_by), "body_edits": list(body_edits),
            "prs": list(prs), "comments": sorted(comments_, key=lambda c: c["created_at"]), "events": sorted(events, key=lambda e: e["at"])}


def ref_pr(url, created_at, state="OPEN", draft=False, merged=False, author=LOGIN, base_ref="main"):
    return {"number": int(url.rsplit("/", 1)[1]), "url": url, "state": state, "draft": draft, "merged": merged, "created_at": created_at,
            "merged_at": None, "closed_at": None, "author": author, "base_ref": base_ref}


def observed(url, state="OPEN", draft=False, merged=False, issues=(A9,), author=LOGIN, base_ref="main", created_at=None):
    """issues.observe_pr の結果 (pr_states の値) の形。"""
    return {"status": "ok", "author": author, "pr": {"url": url, "state": state, "draft": draft, "merged": merged, "base_ref": base_ref,
                                                      "created_at": created_at or t(20), "issues": [{"key": k, "state": "OPEN"} for k in issues]}}


ASSIGN1 = mcomment("割り当て", {"to": W7, "assignment": 1}, t(10), 100)
ASSIGN2 = mcomment("割り当て", {"to": W7, "assignment": 2}, t(200), 200)


class AssignmentTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_no_assignment_comment_means_not_assigned_even_with_field(self):
        """コメント `割り当て` が無ければ、フィールドに ID があっても割り当て中ではない (出どころはコメント。KTD19)。"""
        s = itemstate.derive(make_item(), LOGIN, {}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertIsNone(s["assignment"])
        self.assertFalse(s["assigned"])

    def test_latest_assignment_comment_is_current(self):
        """今の割り当ては最新の `割り当て` (宛先と番号)。前の割り当ての `解放` は数えない。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN1, mcomment("解放", {"to": W7, "assignment": 1, "release_reason": "解除"}, t(20), 101), ASSIGN2])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual((s["assignment"]["to"], s["assignment"]["number"], s["assignment"]["comment_id"]), (W7, 2, 200))
        self.assertIsNone(s["release"])
        self.assertTrue(s["assigned"])

    def test_release_with_current_number_ends_assignment(self):
        """今の番号の `解放` があれば割り当ては終わり (理由と時刻を返す)。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN1, mcomment("解放", {"to": W7, "assignment": 1, "release_reason": "close"}, t(20), 101)], state="CLOSED")
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual(s["release"]["reason"], "close")
        self.assertEqual(s["end"], {"kind": "released", "at": t(20), "reason": "close"})
        self.assertFalse(s["assigned"])

    def test_comments_by_other_authors_are_ignored(self):
        """書き手がトークンのログインと違う先頭行のコメントは、この仕組みのコメントとして扱わない (R6)。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[mcomment("割り当て", {"to": W7, "assignment": 1}, t(10), 100, author="someone")])
        self.assertIsNone(itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {}, PROJECT_NUMBER)["assignment"])

    def test_status_todo_does_not_end_assignment(self):
        """Status だけの `Todo`・`Done` は終わりでも reopen でもない (KTD19)。"""
        item = make_item(status="Todo", comments_=[ASSIGN1])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertTrue(s["assigned"])
        self.assertIsNone(s["end"])


class PrTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_pr_report_url_is_current_pr(self):
        """今の割り当ての PR は、今の割り当ての最新の `PR の報告` の URL の PR。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN1, wcomment("PR の報告", None, t(30), 300, body=PR9), wcomment("PR の報告", None, t(40), 301, body=PR10)],
                         prs=[ref_pr(PR9, t(25))])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {PR9: observed(PR9), PR10: observed(PR10)}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual((s["pr"]["url"], s["pr"]["source"], s["pr"]["closing"]), (PR10, "report", True))

    def test_pr_report_without_closing_reference(self):
        """報告の PR が Issue を閉じる参照を持たなければ closing は偽 (本文の追記を頼む材料。In review にしない)。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN1, wcomment("PR の報告", None, t(30), 300, body=PR9)])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {PR9: observed(PR9, issues=())}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual((s["pr"]["url"], s["pr"]["closing"]), (PR9, False))

    def test_pr_report_of_other_author_is_ignored_then_reference_is_used(self):
        """`PR の報告` の PR の作者がログインと違えば無いものとし、閉じる参照の PR (作者がログイン、作成が割り当ての後) を使う。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN1, wcomment("PR の報告", None, t(30), 300, body=PR10)], prs=[ref_pr(PR9, t(25))])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {PR10: observed(PR10, author="other")}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual((s["pr"]["url"], s["pr"]["source"], s["pr"]["closing"]), (PR9, "reference", True))

    def test_reference_pr_before_assignment_or_by_other_author_is_not_counted(self):
        """前の割り当ての PR (作成が今の `割り当て` より前) と、作者が違う PR は数えない。候補が複数なら作成が最新のもの。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN2], prs=[ref_pr(PR9, t(25), merged=True, state="MERGED"), ref_pr(PR10, t(210), author="other"),
                                                   ref_pr(f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/11", t(220)), ref_pr(f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/12", t(230), draft=True)])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual(s["pr"]["url"], f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/12")

    def test_pr_unreadable_is_reported_as_problem(self):
        """`PR の報告` の PR が読めなければ、PR は無いものとせず、読めなかったことを problems で返し、閉じる参照の PR には戻らない。"""
        item = make_item(comments_=[ASSIGN1, wcomment("PR の報告", None, t(30), 300, body=PR9)], prs=[ref_pr(PR10, t(25))])
        s = itemstate.derive(item, LOGIN, {PR9: {"status": "error", "message": "HTTP 502"}}, PROJECT_NUMBER)
        self.assertEqual((s["pr"], [p["what"] for p in s["problems"]]), (None, ["pr-unreadable"]))

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_SCRIPTS = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "scripts")
sys.path.insert(0, _SCRIPTS)
sys.path.insert(0, _HERE)

from issue_dispatch import comments, config, itemstate  # noqa: E402
from test_project import FakeGhCase, fixture_json  # noqa: E402

_CLI = os.path.join(_SCRIPTS, "issue_dispatch.py")
_DOC = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "skills", "issue-dispatch", "references", "flow.md")

A1, A2, A9 = f"{A}#1", f"{A}#2", f"{A}#9"
LOGIN = "akm"
W7, M1 = "W-7", "M-1"
PR9 = f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/9"
PR10 = f"https://github.com/{A}/pull/10"
PROJECT_NUMBER = 3
_T = ["2026-10-20T00:00:00Z"]


def t(minutes):
    """基準から minutes 分後の時刻 (ISO 8601、UTC)。"""
    return f"2026-10-20T{minutes // 60:02d}:{minutes % 60:02d}:00Z"


def mcomment(kind, values=None, at=None, cid=None, body="", role="manager", name="mgr", sid=M1, author=LOGIN):
    """先頭行付きのコメント (project.items の comments の要素の形)。"""
    line = comments.format_header(role, name, sid, kind, values or {})
    return {"id": f"IC_{cid}", "database_id": cid, "url": f"https://github.com/{A}/issues/9#issuecomment-{cid}",
            "created_at": at, "author": author, "body": f"{line}\n\n{body}" if body else line}


def wcomment(kind, values=None, at=None, cid=None, body="", name="worker 1", sid=W7, author=LOGIN):
    return mcomment(kind, values, at, cid, body, role="worker", name=name, sid=sid, author=author)


def decl_body(files=(("src/a.py", None),), resources=(), split=False):
    obj = {"files": [{"path": p, "units": u} for p, u in files], "resources": list(resources),
           "split": {"needed": True, "reason": "大きい", "remaining": "残り", "blocked_by": []} if split else {"needed": False, "reason": ""}}
    return "```json\n" + json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n```"


def make_item(key=A9, state="OPEN", status="In Progress", session_field=W7, comments_=(), events=(), prs=(), labels=(), assignees=("akm",),
              body_edits=(), position=1, blocked_by=()):
    return {"item_id": "I9", "position": position, "key": key, "repo": key.split("#")[0], "number": int(key.split("#")[1]),
            "url": f"https://github.com/{key.replace('#', '/issues/')}", "state": state, "created_at": t(0), "author": "akm",
            "status": {"name": status, "option_id": "o", "updated_at": t(1)} if status else None,
            "fields": {"Agent session ID": {"text": session_field, "updated_at": t(1)}} if session_field is not None else {},
            "assignees": list(assignees), "labels": list(labels), "blocked_by": list(blocked_by), "body_edits": list(body_edits),
            "prs": list(prs), "comments": sorted(comments_, key=lambda c: c["created_at"]), "events": sorted(events, key=lambda e: e["at"])}


def ref_pr(url, created_at, state="OPEN", draft=False, merged=False, author=LOGIN, base_ref="main"):
    return {"number": int(url.rsplit("/", 1)[1]), "url": url, "state": state, "draft": draft, "merged": merged, "created_at": created_at,
            "merged_at": None, "closed_at": None, "author": author, "base_ref": base_ref}


def observed(url, state="OPEN", draft=False, merged=False, issues=(A9,), author=LOGIN, base_ref="main", created_at=None):
    """issues.observe_pr の結果 (pr_states の値) の形。"""
    return {"status": "ok", "author": author, "pr": {"url": url, "state": state, "draft": draft, "merged": merged, "base_ref": base_ref,
